dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: #{M#Sir}{F#Ma'am}, once you've finished testing the "Saury-Saury Scout," if you have any feedback, please don't hesitate to let me know... even if you think it's terrible!

choices.text: Isn't it a little strange to address me as such?

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Strange? What do you mean?

choices.text: When it comes to being a knight, you have more experience than me.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Ah... You're right, I've never called you that before. It might have made you uncomfortable. I won't do it again!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: It's just... during the International Cross Country Challenge, I met several friends from Natlan and heard of your legendary deeds from a completely new perspective.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: You triumphed in the face of catastrophe and emerged as a great hero of Natlan. You worked side by side with people whose prowess is on a level I never thought possible...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Both your adventures and the way you treat people are so impressive. I admire everything you've accomplished. Your achievements shine as bright as the stars!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Compared to that, I feel like I haven't made much progress at all lately...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: It feels like before, I was striving just to catch up with you, but now your progress is so fast you're almost out of sight...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: #So, it just felt natural to start calling you {M#sir}{F#ma'am}...

choices.text: Don't be so hard on yourself! You'll get stronger too!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Oh... Thanks! I'll definitely keep honing my skills. Gotta keep pushing myself!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: But just burying my head in training and relying solely on diligence... doesn't seem like the right approach either. I need to change my mindset.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: I'm gonna try to find more opportunities to experience new things, to break away from fixed ways of thinking...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: And this collaborative effort to improve the "Saury-Saury Scout" is a great place to start!

choices.text: Who cares about experience — we're friends, aren't we?
Won't these survey devices put you out of a job?

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: The battle between mechanisms and people... I've actually pondered this issue before.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: When I was in Nod-Krai, I read three books written by engineers from Fontaine and Liyue — they gave me quite a few insights.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Mechanisms with unlimited energy that can be controlled from a distance could indeed replace surveyors like me — and maybe even other knights with different roles.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: One of our fellow knights, after studying Fontaine's Gardemeks, once told me, "There will come a day when wars are fought by unmanned mechanisms, without the need for knights or soldiers."

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: But that would require perfect operating conditions. Even if you only consider power supply and operational strategies, there are clear issues that mechanisms alone are unable to solve.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Most mechanisms can't simply deploy from a base, reach a target location, and then begin their mission. If they did, who knows how much of their stored energy would be depleted before the mission even began?

choices.text: That's a good point... There are too many uncertainties along the way.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: That's true. Generally, the operator needs to transport the mechanism to a suitable location before putting it to work. The whole mission is then kept under human supervision in case unexpected circumstances arise.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: In order to produce a mechanism that can work without supervision, a lot more research and development is required.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: So I'm inclined to think that... when it comes to military and adventure applications, mechanisms remain a tool for multiplying human capabilities, rather than a replacement.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: I'd also like to train myself to operate multiple mechanisms by myself to synchronize the survey of larger areas.

choices.text: It's not safe to let mechanisms act independently.
We can talk about that later. Have you been busy lately?

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Ah... Thank you for your concern! As you can see, I'm not too busy right now.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: After helping Vice Captain Lohen's old company adjust to their new duties, I came to help with the cross-country challenge. As for the make-up of the next expedition team, personnel assignment should be scheduled for two weeks' time.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Right. Lohen is the vice captain of the Fifth Company. He was a long-time member of the expedition team, playing a vital role in the mobile contingent.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Recently, the team's mission has changed, and some members of the company are preparing to return to Mondstadt...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: The Fifth Company is a rather special unit. When first formed, they primarily used bows, but as technology has advanced, they've begun equipping themselves with other forms of ranged weaponry...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Normally, they train together as a single unit, but when deployed on missions, they're regularly split into smaller squads and attached to other companies to bolster their firepower.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: The Grand Master said this would make our firepower more flexible. By splitting them up, it ensures no single company finds itself outmatched by long-range opponents.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: As a result, the members of the Fifth Company are "always on standby, ready to deploy to the thick of the action." It means their missions are usually quite challenging.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: And even within Fifth Company, Vice Captain Lohen really stands out. He loves going wherever the fighting is thickest and often complains that there aren't enough monsters. I really admire his fighting spirit!

choices.text: He sounds like quite a character... How does he treat you?

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: He treats me very well! Every time I finish a survey, he insists on verifying the results with me and organizing the intelligence right away...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: If there are any gaps in the survey data, the Vice Captain takes it upon himself to perform "armed recon" to get me the most precise information possible.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: As for his practical jokes... once you get used to them, they're not so bad.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: He has a knack for influencing his closest companions — they all tend to favor his preferred tactic of overwhelming assaults, sometimes even neglecting their own safety...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: So, when it comes to personnel management, beyond just finding the right role that allows them to flourish, they also need to be paired with teammates who can temper their more reckless nature...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: This way, they won't get carried away and use overwhelming force on run-of-the-mill, routine missions.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Once you meet Vice Captain Lohen, you'll understand him a lot better...

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: For some reason, I feel like the two of you are going to hit it off and end up becoming a perfect match!

choices.text: By which I mean... how do you two get along?
I need to give it some thought.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: I—I'll look forward to it!
